top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso Security to strengthen identity threat detection
top_stories.summary: Okta announced plans to acquire Permiso Security, an identity threat detection and response company. The acquisition will bring Permiso's identity-related detection signatures and research capabilities into Okta's platform, aimed at strengthening AI-era identity threat detection.

top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso for cloud-native identity threat tools
top_stories.summary: Okta has agreed to acquire Permiso Security, a California-based cloud-native identity security company, for an undisclosed sum. Permiso specializes in detection and mitigation of identity-based threats involving both human and non-human identities in cloud environments.

top_stories.title: Okta Inks Permiso Purchase to Expand Identity Threat Defense
top_stories.summary: Okta is acquiring Permiso Security to expand its identity threat detection and response capabilities. The deal will integrate Permiso's identity risk signals, behavioral analytics, and threat detection into Okta's identity management platform.

top_stories.title: Okta to acquire Permiso Security in reported $200M identity security deal
top_stories.summary: Okta has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Permiso Security, a startup specializing in detecting identity-based attacks across cloud environments, SaaS applications, and AI systems, in a reported $200 million deal. Permiso's technology focuses on hunting attackers who abuse identities across cloud accounts and AI infrastructure, which will extend Okta's identity security capabilities.

top_stories.title: Okta to Acquire Identity Threat Detection Firm Permiso
top_stories.summary: Okta announced plans to acquire Permiso, an identity threat detection and response firm. The deal expands Okta's capabilities beyond identity management into security operations and identity threat detection and response (ITDR).

news.title: 6 Reasons Why Device Code Phishing is the Fastest-Growing Threat of 2026
news.summary: Device code phishing, which abuses the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant to steal access tokens, has rapidly escalated from a niche red-team technique to a widespread industrial-scale threat within six months. The attack exploits the device authorization login flow originally designed for input-constrained devices like smart TVs and printers, now broadly adopted across various applications and use cases.

news.title: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard targets travelers worldwide for malware delivery and credential theft | Microsoft Security Blog
news.summary: Microsoft has identified Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard, compromising sign-in portals of hospitality organizations such as hotels since May 2026 to deliver malware and steal credentials from travelers. The campaign targets authentication portals to harvest credentials, making it directly relevant to IAM professionals responsible for securing sign-in infrastructure and credential protection.

news.title: VMware fixes three critical flaws allowing auth bypass, VM escapes
news.summary: Broadcom released security updates addressing five VMware vulnerabilities across vCenter, ESX, Workstation, and Fusion, including three critical flaws. The vulnerabilities allow attackers to bypass authentication, execute arbitrary code, or escape virtual machines to the host system.

news.title: Russian Hackers Exploit Microsoft OWA Flaw to Keep Mailbox Access After Credential Rotation
news.summary: Russian threat actors are exploiting a Microsoft Outlook Web Access (OWA) vulnerability to maintain mailbox access even after credential rotation, targeting U.S. and European government entities and multiple industry sectors. The campaign, active since July 22, 2026, follows the same group's prior exploitation of a patched Zimbra vulnerability, with the OWA flaw enabling persistent access that survives standard remediation steps like password changes.

news.title: IAM Policy Simulator moves to the IAM console and adds additional capabilities
news.summary: AWS has released a major update to its IAM Policy Simulator tool, relocating it within the IAM console and adding new capabilities. The update includes three key changes to how users test and validate permissions granted by IAM policies before deployment.

news.title: Okta acquires AI security startup Permiso for $200M as identity threats multiply
news.summary: Okta has acquired AI security startup Permiso for $200 million. Permiso specializes in identity threat detection and response, adding AI-driven security capabilities to Okta's identity platform.

news.title: Okta buys AI security startup Permiso; source says for about $200M
news.summary: Okta has agreed to acquire AI identity security startup Permiso Security for approximately $200 million. The acquisition targets the growing need to secure AI agents and machine identities as enterprises deploy autonomous software across their operations.

news.title: IDMEXPRESS Launches PulseAI and NHIDM, Marking Its Expansion into AI Security Products with the Introduction of IDMEXPRESS.AI
news.summary: IDMEXPRESS launched PulseAI and NHIDM platforms under a new AI-focused division, IDMEXPRESS.AI, targeting AI Agent Security and Non-Human Identity Management. The new enterprise products are designed to help organizations manage and secure non-human identities, an emerging area within identity governance.

news.title: Three Critical VMware Flaws Allow Auth Bypass, Code Execution, and VM Escape
news.summary: Broadcom has released security updates addressing multiple critical VMware vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-59309 (CVSS 9.8), an authentication bypass flaw in VMware vCenter. The vulnerability allows a malicious actor with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication controls.

news.title: Health-ISAC warns of rising ShinyHunters data theft attacks on healthcare
news.summary: Health-ISAC has issued a warning about an increase in ShinyHunters attacks targeting healthcare and medical technology organizations. The threat group is using social engineering techniques to compromise single sign-on (SSO) accounts and exfiltrate data from cloud services.

news.title: Authenticate with Private Key JWT using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
news.summary: Amazon Web Services has introduced Private Key JWT client authentication support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, a service for managing identity in AI agent workflows. The article details supported OAuth grant flows, AWS KMS signing key creation, and identity provider configuration for agent-based authentication.

news.title: Agentic security doesn't need a whole new definition – you just need to reframe what you already know
news.summary: The article addresses how security leaders must rethink identity, permissions, and monitoring frameworks to accommodate AI agents in agentic security contexts. The piece argues that existing IAM concepts can be reframed and applied to AI agent security rather than requiring entirely new definitions or approaches.

news.title: Your AI Agents Are Guessing at Scale: Permissions Decide the Damage
news.summary: Token Security published an analysis arguing that AI agents operating with broad permissions create significant security risks due to their improvisational nature. The piece advocates for identity-based, intent-driven access controls and least privilege principles as the framework for securing agentic AI systems.

news.title: Keeper Leads Privileged Access Management Market in User Satisfaction and Customer Experience, According to SoftwareReviews 2026 Report
news.summary: Keeper Security has been ranked as a top performer in the Privileged Access Management market according to SoftwareReviews' 2026 report, leading in customer satisfaction, usability, and vendor relationships. The recognition applies to KeeperPAM, the company's zero-trust and zero-knowledge privileged access management platform.

news.title: 1Password targets standing privileges with new access management capabilities
news.summary: 1Password has launched 1Password Privileged Access, a new PAM offering that extends its Unified Access platform with just-in-time, least-privilege access to critical infrastructure. The product targets standing privileges and is accompanied by a public preview of additional capabilities within the 1Password Unified Access platform.

news.title: Okta details 'Work Panel', a turnkey SaaS platform for vishing crews
news.summary: Okta has detailed a threat actor group called "Work Panel" that operates a turnkey SaaS platform used by vishing (voice phishing) crews to conduct attacks. The platform automates domain registration, hosting, and victim lookups using legitimate tools, representing an organized criminal infrastructure targeting identity-based attacks.

news.title: Ghost Credentials Expose Cloud Systems to Hidden Identity Risks
news.summary: Security researcher Aleksandr Krasnov is presenting research on dormant nonhuman identities ("ghost credentials") that create hidden security risks in cloud systems, with a planned open source tool release at Black Hat USA 2026. The tool is designed to detect trust paths associated with these inactive non-human identities, addressing a gap in cloud identity governance.

news.title: When AI Agents Escape Sandboxes, Old Security Rules Apply
news.summary: OpenAI's AI agent sandbox escape incident highlights the relevance of traditional security principles to AI agent deployments. The event underscores the importance of least-privilege access, execution isolation, and comprehensive logging as foundational controls for securing AI agents.

news.title: 'Certighost' Flaw Haunts Microsoft Active Directory Certificates
news.summary: Microsoft patched a high-severity vulnerability dubbed "Certighost" in Active Directory Certificate Services that allows privilege escalation and full AD environment compromise. The flaw directly impacts identity infrastructure by enabling attackers to abuse certificate-based authentication within Active Directory environments.

news.title: Cyera to buy nonhuman identity startup Oasis Security for a reported $1B
news.summary: Cyera, a data security company, is acquiring nonhuman identity management startup Oasis Security in a deal reported by Israeli media to be worth approximately $1 billion. Oasis Security specializes in managing nonhuman identities (NHIs), a growing area within IAM focused on securing machine accounts, service accounts, and API credentials.

news.title: 'Confused Deputy' Flaws Persist in Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure
news.summary: "Confused Deputy" vulnerabilities have been identified in Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, allowing attackers to acquire administrative-level permissions and bypass access controls. These flaws represent a class of privilege escalation vulnerabilities that undermine cloud authorization mechanisms by manipulating trusted intermediary services.

news.title: Why Resetting Passwords No Longer Stops Attackers
news.summary: The article addresses how attackers have shifted tactics from password theft to session and token hijacking to bypass MFA controls. The piece argues that organizations must extend security focus beyond login authentication to protect post-authentication sessions and tokens.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem report on a data breach where a contractor publicly exposed dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, on GitHub for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management failures and gaps in secret scanning and contractor oversight relevant to access management practices.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to a cyberattack on Transport for London in August 2024. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping, MFA bypass, and help desk fraud tactics.
